account:
It is day 0, shortly after fourteen. I have followed my appointments: morning office business, a market walk, lunch at home, and now town accounts. My market enquiries uncovered no confirmed unusual news. Several townspeople saw the baker carrying wheat at the bakery; the baker told me thirty-two fresh loaves were stocked and asked whether upcoming town gatherings would need bread. That could simply be ordinary business, and I know of no gathering requiring an order.

The one engagement I know little about is tea at fifteen with someone called neighbour. The secretary visited them and confirmed the invitation at the east-bank dockside cottage, coordinates sixteen, one hundred five, and filed a separate confirmation in the appointments chest. Tea is also in tomorrow's appointment book. I intend to attend, but I have no evidence yet that it is anything other than a social visit.

The secretary reports no new correspondence, reported outstanding payments, council matters, unusual expenses, or funding requests, but has not examined account records and does not know where they are. I do not currently know their location either. The treasury contains two stacks of sixty-four emeralds and no account documents. This leaves today's financial review incomplete, not evidence of wrongdoing. I still feel I may be missing something in town, but nothing I have personally seen or heard establishes a secret activity, its participants, or its purpose.
